subject: Retainer retune & invoice latch discussion
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchardanalytics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal coming up — looking to retune our retainer

Hi Rafael,

Our renewal for the retainer is due in May and usage has been notably lumpy since Q1. We’re evaluating whether to move more to a committed retainer or keep a hybrid model; finance is worried about large invoice variance. Two asks from our side: a) can you surface options that smooth monthly invoice swings (we call it an "invoice latch" internally), and b) given expected growth, what uplift discounts or temporary rate holds could you offer if we sign a 12–18 month commit now?

I attached our Q1 usage export for context.

Can we get a short call next week to map options? Tom (CC) will be on finance.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform & Ops
Orchard Analytics

Attachment: orchard_usage_q1-2027.csv
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchardanalytics.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@orchardanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — looking to retune our retainer

Hi Elena — thanks for the context and the file.

Short answer: yes — we can design a ‘retainer retune’ that smooths invoices and gives staged price protection as you scale. High-level options I’d like to walk through on a call:
- Monthly invoice latch: a three-month trailing average that defines a baseline invoice with overage true-ups quarterly (reduces month-to-month swings).
- Tempo discount: an initial short-term uplift discount (6 months) tied to a modest committed uplift, then a measured step to the committed rate — helps with forecast windows.
- Growth collar: a safety band that automatically increases committed capacity at a pre-agreed rate when you exceed thresholds, with pre-negotiated unit pricing.

I’m attaching a proposed term sheet (draft v3) that maps each option to pricing and operational triggers. If you want, I can include an invoice timing amendment for PO/invoice latch language.

Available for a 30-min call Tue/Wed next week — what works for you?

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchardanalytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@orchardanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — looking to retune our retainer

Looping in for pricing alignment and legal-read flags. Rafael, I like the three levers you sketched. Two pragmatic negotiating notes from our side:
1) If Orchard signs a 12–18 month committed uplift at <= 15% above Q1 run-rate, we can offer a one-time onboarding credit (applied against first two invoices) and a 60-day invoice hold for the first quarter to smooth cash flow.
2) We can add a fallback to a slightly lower-performing but cheaper model variant (same API) for burst periods — preserves SLA but lowers unit cost when you’re above the growth collar.

Elena/Tom — we can have legal draft a short invoice latch amendment to attach to the order form; Rafael will circulate pricing bands before the call so we can go into numbers.

-Marissa
VP, Customer Success & Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Becker <tom.becker@orchardanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchardanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — looking to retune our retainer

Thanks — quick clarifying Qs from finance:
1) How would the invoice latch interact with our existing PO cadence? We need invoices aligned to our net-30 payment schedule and prefer predictable month-ends for forecasting.
2) Regarding the onboarding credit — is that a one-time dollar credit or percent off first invoices? We’d prefer a dollar credit tied to predicted incremental spend.

Also, can you confirm the unit price delta if we use the cheaper model variant during bursts? We need to model worst-case spend if bursts persist.

If it helps, we’re prepared to commit to an initial 12-month uplift of +12% over Q1 baseline if you can lock pricing for the first 9 months.

Tom Becker
Director of Finance, Orchard Analytics
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchardanalytics.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@orchardanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T16:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — looking to retune our retainer

Elena / Tom — great, thanks for the commitment signal. Action items and confirmations below so everyone is aligned:

1) Invoice latch: we’ll draft an amendment that defines the baseline as the greater of (a) three-month trailing average, or (b) agreed Q1 baseline. Invoices will be issued monthly on your existing PO cadence; overages/credits reconciled quarterly with a net-30 payment window.

2) Onboarding credit: one-time fixed credit of $45,000 applied across your first two invoices after the new term begins (we’ll show the dollar credit in the term sheet).

3) Pricing hold: Redwood will hold unit pricing for the first 9 months at the agreed uplift rate (+12% vs Q1 baseline). After 9 months pricing steps are recalibrated based on actual run-rate and the growth collar triggers.

4) Cheaper model variant for bursts: delta is -18% unit cost vs primary model. We’ll include a simple cost model in the updated term sheet so you can stress-test worst-case spend.

Next steps: Rafael will attach updated term sheet (v4) with the dollar-credit line and invoice latch language and a short cost-model appendix. Marissa will have legal prep an amendment to the order form and Kimberly will surface ops items for burst routing. If that all looks good, I’ll send a DocuSign link for signature.

Proposed next call: 2027-04-26 at 10:00am PT to finalize.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
